name: גְּדַלְיָהוּ
summary: Five men bear it. The chief is Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, whom Nebuchadnezzar set over the people left in Judah after Jerusalem fell; Jeremiah went to live with him at Mizpah, and in the seventh month Ishmael son of Nethaniah struck him down (2Ki 25:22, 25; Jer 40:5–41:2). The others are Gedaliah son of Pashhur, one of the officials who heard Jeremiah's words (Jer 38:1); Zephaniah's great-grandfather, son of Amariah (Zep 1:1); a priest of the sons of Jeshua who had married a foreign woman (Ezr 10:18); and a son of Jeduthun, who led the second lot of singers in David's day (1Ch 25:3, 9). It is spelled גְּדַלְיָהוּ and גְּדַלְיָה. The name is the qal of גָּדַל with the divine name: “Yah is great”, the confession David makes to Yahweh, גָּדַלְתָּ “you are great” (2Sa 7:22; Psa 104:1).

evidence.note: Nebuchadnezzar “appointed over them גְּדַלְיָהוּ בֶּן־אֲחִיקָם בֶּן־שָׁפָן”.
Ishmael son of Nethaniah struck Gedaliah, and he died.
“Return to גְּדַלְיָה son of Ahikam … whom the king of Babylon has appointed over the cities of Judah.”
Zephaniah son of Cushi son of גְּדַלְיָה son of Amariah.
The sons of Jeduthun: גְּדַלְיָהוּ and Zeri and Jeshaiah …
“Therefore גָּדַלְתָּ, my Lord Yahweh”: the verb of the name, said of Yahweh.
“Yahweh my God, you are very great (גָּדַלְתָּ).”

note: BDB lists the same 32 tokens under c.aq.ai (גְּדַלְיָה) and c.aq.aj (גְּדַלְיָהוּ); only c.aq.aj is named. The verb could be read as a perfect, “Yah is (or has become) great”; scripture gives no explanation of the name.
